questions.q: Vouvray Moelleux, one of the Loire's sweet wines, is made from which grape?
questions.exp: Vouvray, east of Tours in Touraine, is a Chenin Blanc appellation (a token share of Orbois is allowed), and in warm autumns with noble rot or shrivelled berries growers make moelleux beside their sec, demi-sec and sparkling wines. The Court lists it with Quarts de Chaume and Bonnezeaux, both Chenin too, as the Loire's noble rot appellations.

questions.q: By the Court's rule, the frozen grapes for Eiswein and Icewine must be free of which fungal infection?
questions.exp: Eiswein and Icewine come from healthy grapes left to freeze on the vine and pressed while frozen, so the water stays behind as ice and the juice is concentrated. The Court's rule is that the fruit be free of noble rot, whose honey, saffron and ginger would blur the pure fruit and searing acidity that mark the style.

questions.q: Recioto della Valpolicella, the sweet red made from dried grapes, is made chiefly from which variety?
questions.exp: Corvina leads the Valpolicella blend with Rondinella, and for Recioto its bunches are dried for months before pressing, then fermented only part way so the wine stays sweet. Garganega makes the white Recioto di Soave and Trebbiano, with Malvasia, makes Vin Santo, the Court's other two dried grape wines.

questions.q: Besides the white grapes Vidal and Riesling, which red grape does the Court name for Canadian Icewine?
questions.exp: Ontario's Icewine is mostly Vidal, a winter hardy hybrid, with Riesling for the finest whites, and Cabernet Franc gives a pink to pale red Icewine with strawberry and red berry notes. Under VQA the grapes must freeze naturally on the vine and be picked at minus 8°C or colder.

questions.q: By the Court's guide, which of these formats ages a sweet wine best over many years?
questions.exp: The Court notes that full-sized bottles age better than half bottles: the larger volume holds proportionally less of the air under the cork and changes temperature more slowly, so a 750 ml Sauternes develops more slowly and evenly than a 375. Many sweet wines are bottled in clear glass, so they must also be kept out of direct light.

questions.q: Which Sauternes estate was ranked a Premier Cru in the 1855 classification?
questions.exp: Château Rieussec, in Fargues, is one of the Premiers Crus that sit below Château d'Yquem, the sole Premier Cru Supérieur; Filhot, Doisy-Daëne and de Malle are Deuxièmes Crus. The Court asks a couple of producers in each category, to recommend in service.

questions.q: By the Court's standard, how many ounces make the usual by the glass pour of a sweet wine?
questions.exp: The Court sets a by the glass serving of sweet wine at 2 oz, about 59 ml, so a 375 ml half bottle gives six glasses and a 750 ml bottle about twelve. Kept cold in the refrigerator, an opened bottle can typically last for a week.

questions.q: In what bottle size is Tokaji Aszú often sold, the figure a sommelier must use to cost a glass correctly?
questions.exp: Tokaji Aszú usually comes in a 500 ml bottle, so at the Court's 2 oz pour it gives about eight glasses rather than the twelve of a 750 ml bottle. Costing it as a 750 would understate the cost of each glass by about a third.
